label: prop:coxeter-tits-residue-collapse
title: The Tits residue collapsed: cell faithfulness is simple-distinctness
html:
Proposition. The Tits residue collapsed: cell faithfulness is simple-distinctness

Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system and s_i, s_j a generator pair with m_{ij} = 3 (respectively m_{ij} = 2). Then

[s_i, s_j, s_i] \text{ is reduced}
\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
s_i \neq s_j

(respectively [s_i, s_j] is reduced \Leftrightarrow s_i \neq s_j).

The forward direction is elementary. For the converse the reflection cocycle is used quantitatively: pairwise-distinct reflections t with cocycle value \eta(w, t) = 1 bound the length of w from below, because each such reflection occurs in the inversion sequence of any reduced word for w. The inversion sequence of the cell word is computed in closed form — [\,s_j,\; s_i s_j s_i,\; s_i\,] at m_{ij} = 3, the first entry collapsing by the braid relation, and [\,s_i,\; s_j\,] at m_{ij} = 2 — and simple-distinctness makes its entries pairwise distinct, forcing \ell \geq the word length.

Consequently the parabolic transversals, and with them the braid and far-commutation relations on the length-rule module, require only s_i \neq s_j per pair: nothing about lengths or words survives in the residue. What remains of Tits faithfulness, per generator pair, is exactly injectivity of the simple-reflection map — the point where the geometric representation classically enters, and which it settles unconditionally (simple-injectivity).
